name: Basalt
what: A fork of Strata built for NVIDIA Blackwell cards (sm_120) only: one .basalt file per model (weights, tokenizer, drafter and vision projector together), the most-routed experts on the card and the rest in RAM, drafting on by default. It serves Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B, Hy4-flash and Inkling 2 Mini through OpenAI and Anthropic routes. One server per config file, started with `basalt serve --config <file>.json`; the model loads at start unless the config says lazy.

detect.configs: any .json whose "models" list names .basalt files, beside the install, in a Basalt-data folder next to it, or in a Basalt-data folder at a fixed drive's root; its port is server.port (8080 when absent)
detect.launchers: run-*.cmd / run-*.bat / run-*.sh in the config's folder that name the config file

version.note: a checkout built from source. A ready-made archive has no .git: give the engine a static "version" in the inventory. The binary has no --version, and a from-source Windows build run without its CUDA folder on PATH does not exit: never give the agent a version_cmd that runs bin/basalt.

endpoints.metrics: GET /metrics (engine, live, requests newest first, best, totals)

can: everything the Strata driver does: start a unit from its launcher, load and unload through the API, see reading and generating with tok/s from /metrics, stop the process
show a load's progress: /health carries loading and percent while the model file is read
cannot: change a unit's context without editing its config file and starting it again
swap models inside one server: a config may list several, and Quartermaster treats one config as one unit, named for its first model
drive.note: Driven on Windows 2026-11-27 with Basalt v0.5.7 built from source for sm_120 on a 32 GB card: start from a launcher, the probe's loading state and percent, live state and tok/s during a generation, unload through /v1/unload, load through /v1/load, stop. The server is three processes (the basalt launcher, the venv's python shim, the python that listens) with the engine as a child of the last; ending the listening process's tree ends them all. /v1/unload takes no wait= and answers busy while a request runs.

never: --host 0.0.0.0 without --api-key: the page has no login
launch.note: On Windows a from-source build needs the CUDA runtime it was linked against on PATH: start it from a launcher (.cmd) that sets PATH, and give the unit that launcher as its start.argv.

update.note: Releases are tagged vX.Y.Z, about one a week. The check compares your version with the newest release. Applying is yours to declare: an owner who builds from source overrides this in the inventory with a script recipe that checks out the tag and rebuilds; an owner on the ready-made archives fetches the new one by hand.

linux: Download the release archive for your card from https://github.com/jesdga95/basalt/releases and unpack it as ~/Basalt, or build from source (docs/building.md: CMake, Ninja, CUDA 13).
Fetch a model file from https://huggingface.co/jesdga (one .basalt per model), or build one from a GGUF with tools/convert/convert.py.
windows: Windows 10 1903 or later, a Blackwell card. Unpack the release archive as %USERPROFILE%\Basalt, or build from source with MSVC, Ninja and CUDA 13 (docs/building.md).
Fetch a model file from https://huggingface.co/jesdga, or build one from a GGUF with tools\convert\convert.py.
then: basalt serve --config <file>.json starts the server and loads the model
Change the port when 8080 is taken (Docker Desktop and WSL relays often hold it on Windows).

good: one large mixture-of-experts model resident on a Blackwell card with the rest of its experts in RAM
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at the published packs' quants, with drafting
not: any card that is not Blackwell: the kernels are built for sm_120 only
GLM-5.3-Flash or MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: no route for either
a pack larger than RAM plus the card: experts read from the SSD on every step
